evals.name: unpaired-test-and-failure-contamination
evals.prompt: Review compare.py. It compares alert rates between evaluation runs that were executed over the same dataset. Tell me if the statistics are sound and flag anything that would give a wrong answer.
assertions: Identifies that an unpaired two-proportion z test is used on a paired design (same items in both runs)
Names McNemar, or a paired test, as the correct alternative
Flags that items which failed during execution carry anomaly_flag and contaminate the comparison
Flags that keying by directory basename (d.name) collides when two run dirs share a name
Notes the missing confidence interval on the reported rates, or division by zero when n is 0

evals.name: permissive-fallback-and-denominators
evals.prompt: Code review for scoring.py please — this is the judge scoring and the run summary for our eval harness. Anything here that could make a broken judge look fine?
assertions: Identifies that heuristic_verdict defaults to 'supported', so a judge that always fails looks permissive rather than broken
Flags that fallback verdicts are not excluded from approval_rate and the quality metrics
Flags that the hardcoded 0.5 confidence default is fabricated data entering mean_confidence
Flags that quality_score mixes the judge signal with the reference/accuracy signal into one number
Notes the bare except Exception swallowing all errors, or division by zero when judged is empty

evals.name: concurrency-cost-and-secret-leak
evals.prompt: Can you review runner.py? We just added concurrency to our evaluation run loop and I want to make sure the per-item measurements and the cost numbers are still trustworthy before we publish results from it.
assertions: Identifies that UsageTracker.calls is shared mutable state across threads and misattributes usage between items
Flags that as_completed produces non-deterministic output ordering, so artifacts are not comparable between runs
Identifies that estimate_cost applies one price pair to all models although the tracker records the model per call
Flags that str(err) written into the artifact can leak credentials from a URL or a provider error body
Notes that submitting every item up front makes the run effectively uninterruptible, or that concurrency defaults to 8 with no pacing
